catalog_quote: Finally, stress in Ende falls on the penultimate syllable, unless the penultimate syllable contains a schwa. In that case, stress falls on the ultimate syllable. Stress is usually marked by an increase in intensity and vowel length. ... [p. 208] the mid-central vowel is phonetically shorter than all other vowels and never takes stress or prominence in the root or the word. ... Lastly, the schwa is limited to the first syllable of bisyllabic words as well as the numeral proclitic sa /sə/ and the prepositional proclitic pa /pə/; that is, it is disallowed in the ultimate syllable. ... [p. 211] The defining characteristics of clitics in Ende are: 1) clitics are one only syllable, 2) clitics have a phonetically short vowel, and 3) clitics are always unstressed. ... audit.reasoning: Quote check: every segment of the deciding quotation (stress rule p. 211, schwa never stressed / barred from the ultima p. 208, clitics always unstressed p. 211, wordlist items 206-215 p. 224) is verbatim in the JSEALS-2 text we hold at the cited pages. The classification (right-edge penult default, final stress when the penult is schwa; class full-vs-reduced-vowel; no secondary stress described; domain word with clitics excluded) follows the source exactly, and the transcribed wordlist independently shows the pattern ([təˈɹu], [səmˈbuɹu] vs [ˈßutu], [səˈŋasu]). Deciding source is a 2009 peer-reviewed phonology article from primary fieldwork and is the sole descriptive reference Glottolog holds for this languoid; no grammar, dissertation or instrumental study of Flores Ende stress was found. sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Comparative treatment of the Central Flores group cited by Glottolog for Ende's subclassification; may contain comparative phonology notes (schwa, stress) for Ende vs. Lio. Leiden student-thesis repository is JS-only (Primo) and could not be downloaded headlessly.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: Same fieldworker's later paper on Ende clitics vs. phonological words (minimal bimoraic word, unstressed monomoraic clitics); the only post-2009 first-hand Ende phonology item found, could refine the clitic/secondary-stress wording of the primary-stress rule/the secondary-stress rule. Unpaywall lists it as OA at journals.linguisticsociety.org/proceedings/index.php/BLS/article/download/3879/3575, but the host could not be reached by automated download/timeouts and web.archive.org was offline when we checked the sources.
